learning_outcomes.text: Knows the concept of fluid and general terminology related to fluids.
Understands the behavior of fluid in a static state.
Learns how to apply Bernoulli's law to fluids.
Can establish the relationship between fluid and energy.
Develops equations describing fluid flow in integral form and solves simple flow problems.
Can perform momentum analysis of fluid systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and basic concepts (fluid concept, no-slip, classification of flows, system and control volume)
Properties of fluids (density, vapor pressure, specific energy, compressibility, viscosity and surface tension)
Fluid statics (pressure and pressure measuring devices, hydrostatic pressure force: plane and curved surfaces, solid body motion: rigid translation and rotation)
Fluid kinematics (Lagrangian & Eulerian approaches, material derivative and acceleration, streamlines-pathlines-streaklines-timelines, Reynolds Transport Theorem)
Integral form of flow analysis (mass conservation equation, energy conservation equation, Bernoulli equation, linear momentum equation and angular momentum equation)
assessment_rules: The overall assessment includes a Midterm Exam (60%), Quiz 1 (20%), and Quiz 2 (20%) for a total of 100% in semester studies. The final grade is determined by 50% from the in-term success and 50% from the Final Exam.
